security_audit.summary: The static command, filesystem, network, and token matches are documentation examples or placeholders in SKILL.md, not executable skill behavior. The main confirmed issue is a semantic workflow security concern: mutable @master action references in the security scanning template. Authors should pin actions, prefer short-lived cloud authentication, and include or remove missing referenced assets.

remediation.suggestion: Pin Trivy and Snyk actions to immutable commit SHAs or reviewed release tags, and update the examples to match the stated versioning guidance.

remediation.issue: Long-lived AWS access key deployment example
remediation.suggestion: Prefer GitHub OIDC with cloud role assumption for AWS deployments, and scope permissions to the minimum required actions.
Set default read-only permissions and add scoped job permissions for packages, deployments, and security event uploads.
Include the referenced asset and resource files or remove those references so users do not rely on missing material.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable GitHub Action References
semantic_findings.description: The security scanning workflow recommends aquasecurity/trivy-action@master and snyk/actions/node@master. Mutable branch references can change without review and create supply-chain risk if copied into production workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly uses two third-party actions pinned to the mutable master branch in a security workflow example. This conflicts with the nearby best practice to use specific action versions.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable workflow templates for testing, packaging, deployment, and security checks. This skill provides reusable GitHub Actions patterns that Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can adapt to a repository.
actual_capabilities: Creates test workflows for Node.js projects with dependency caching, linting, test runs, and coverage upload.
Drafts Docker image build and registry publishing workflows for GitHub Container Registry.
Provides Kubernetes deployment workflows that update kubeconfig, apply manifests, and verify rollout status.
Builds matrix workflows across operating systems and Python versions.
Shows reusable workflow patterns with inputs and secrets.
Adds security scanning and production approval examples.
limitations: Only one SKILL.md file is packaged; referenced asset and resource files are not included.
Examples must be adapted before use in a production repository.
Cloud deployment examples require existing credentials, clusters, namespaces, and permissions.
The skill does not test workflows against a live GitHub repository.

use_cases.title: Create CI for an Application
use_cases.description: Generate a GitHub Actions workflow that installs dependencies, runs lint checks, executes tests, and publishes coverage.

use_cases.title: Publish Container Images
use_cases.description: Build a workflow that tags Docker images and pushes them to GitHub Container Registry after approved changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Workflows
use_cases.description: Create reusable workflow patterns for shared testing, security scanning, and deployment practices across repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Node.js repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow for a Node.js app. It should install dependencies, run linting, run tests, cache npm packages, and upload coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker Publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate release automation for container images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my repository for Docker image builds on main branch pushes and version tags. Use GitHub Container Registry and least-privilege permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Deployment Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that deploys to Kubernetes after tests pass. Include environment approval, rollout verification, and secure cloud authentication notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build Reusable Platform Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reusable GitHub Actions workflows for multiple services. Include typed inputs, secrets handling, matrix tests, security scanning, and guidance for pinning actions.

output_examples.input: Create CI for a Node.js service.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline with checkout, Node setup, npm caching, dependency installation, linting, tests, and coverage upload.

output_examples.input: Publish Docker images to GitHub Container Registry.
output_examples.output: A build plan with registry login, metadata extraction, image build, cache configuration, package write permissions, and tag handling.
A production deployment workflow description with environment approval, deployment commands, notification, and verification steps.

best_practices: Pin third-party actions to immutable SHAs or reviewed version tags.
Set least-privilege permissions at the workflow and job levels.
Use GitHub environments, required reviews, and secure secret storage for production deployments.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example cluster names, namespaces, or secret names without review.
Do not use mutable action refs such as master or latest in production workflows.
Do not expose deployment workflows to untrusted pull request contexts.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates GitHub Actions workflow patterns for testing, Docker publishing, Kubernetes deployment, security scanning, approvals, and matrix builds.

faq.question: Can it deploy to Kubernetes?
faq.answer: It can draft Kubernetes deployment workflows, but you must supply real cluster names, namespaces, credentials, and approval rules.

faq.question: Does it include all referenced template files?
faq.answer: No. The packaged skill contains SKILL.md, while several referenced asset and resource files are not included.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with secrets?
faq.answer: The examples use GitHub secrets placeholders. Review permissions, prefer short-lived credentials, and avoid exposing secrets to untrusted workflows.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace workflow testing?
faq.answer: No. Validate generated workflows in a branch or staging repository before production use.
